## Three tracks

::: {.grid3}
::: {.tile}
### Machine learning engineer
{{< var n_mle >}} postings. Trains models and runs them in production: PyTorch ({{< var p_pytorch_mle >}}%),
production lifecycle ({{< var p_production_ml_mle >}}%), MLOps ({{< var p_mlops_mle >}}%), plus ranking or
autonomy depending on the company.
:::
::: {.tile}
### AI engineer
{{< var n_ai_engineer >}} postings. Builds products on models: agents ({{< var p_agents_ai >}}%), frameworks and
harnesses ({{< var p_orchestration_ai >}}%), backend ({{< var p_backend_ai >}}%), evaluation
({{< var p_evals_ai >}}%).
:::
::: {.tile}
### Research engineer
{{< var n_research_engineer >}} postings. Engineers inside research teams: experiment rigor
({{< var p_experimentation_re >}}%), research code ({{< var p_research_eng_re >}}%), reinforcement learning
({{< var p_rl_re >}}%), large-scale training ({{< var p_dist_training_re >}}%).
:::
:::

## What is here

- **[Report](report/index.qmd)**: what the postings ask for, by track, role type, employer type and level, with
  every skill counted.
- **[Skills](skills/index.qmd)**: one page per area with the demand table, the senior bar, a checklist and the
  questions with answers. **[Design cases](skills/cases.qmd)** are the worked system design rounds.
- **[Review](review/index.qmd)**: the same cards with spaced repetition, mock interview rounds, and a readiness
  figure per track that shows the highest-demand skills you have not covered.
- **[Plan](plan/index.qmd)**: the order of areas per track, a six-week schedule and the daily loop.
- **[Reported questions](report/index.qmd#reported)**: {{< var n_reports >}} questions that candidates report being asked at
  {{< var n_report_companies >}} of these employers, matched to the cards that cover them. Unverified, with a link to each source.
- **[Open roles](jobs/index.qmd)**: the postings themselves, filterable by track, role type and skill.
- **[Notes](notes/index.qmd)**: long-form deep dives from first principles, linked from the skill pages.

## How the notes are written

Each deep-dive note answers four questions:

1. What is the core idea?
2. Can I derive it?
3. Can I implement it in PyTorch?
4. What deep dive questions expose whether I really understand it?
